availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

<script lang="ts">
/**
 * InlineConfirmButton
 *
 * A reusable button component for destructive actions that requires inline confirmation.
 * First click shows confirmation state, second click within 3s triggers the action.
 * Auto-resets after 3s if not confirmed.
 */
import { cn } from '$lib/utils.js';

interface Props {
  /** Initial button label */
  label: string;
  /** Label shown during confirmation state */
  confirmLabel?: string;
  /** Visual variant */
  variant?: 'destructive' | 'warning';
  /** Whether the button is disabled */
  disabled?: boolean;
  /** Callback when action is confirmed */
  onConfirm: () => void | Promise<void>;
  /** Additional CSS classes */
  class?: string;
  /** Test ID for E2E testing */
  testId?: string;
}

const {
  label,
  confirmLabel = 'Confirm?',
  variant = 'destructive',
  disabled = false,
  onConfirm,
  class: className,
  testId,
}: Props = $props();

let confirming = $state(false);
let timeoutId = $state<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);

function clearResetTimeout() {
  if (timeoutId) {
    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
    timeoutId = null;
  }
}

function resetState() {
  confirming = false;
  clearResetTimeout();
}

async function handleClick() {
  if (disabled) return;

  if (confirming) {
    // Second click - confirm the action
    resetState();
    await onConfirm();
  } else {
    // First click - enter confirmation state
    confirming = true;
    // Auto-reset after 3 seconds
    timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
      confirming = false;
      timeoutId = null;
    }, 3000);
  }
}

// Cleanup on unmount
$effect(() => {
  return () => {
    clearResetTimeout();
  };
});

const baseClasses = 'px-3 py-1 text-sm rounded transition-colors font-medium';

const variantClasses = $derived(
  variant === 'destructive'
    ? confirming
      ? 'bg-red-700 text-white hover:bg-red-800'
      : 'bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700'
    : confirming
      ? 'bg-amber-700 text-white hover:bg-amber-800'
      : 'bg-amber-600 text-white hover:bg-amber-700',
);

const disabledClasses = 'opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed';
</script>

<button
  type="button"
  class={cn(baseClasses, variantClasses, disabled && disabledClasses, className)}
  onclick={handleClick}
  {disabled}
  data-testid={testId}
>
  {confirming ? confirmLabel : label}
</button>

content.text:
I now have a thorough picture of the entire daemon. Here is a complete summary of all findings:

---

## Daemon Server Code: Full Analysis

### Framework

The daemon uses **Elysia.js** (a Bun-native HTTP/WebSocket framework) throughout. Routes are defined using method chaining (`.get()`, `.post()`, `.delete()`). No PUT or PATCH methods are used anywhere in the daemon — all mutation endpoints use POST.

---

### Route Registration Index

**File:** `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/server.ts`

This is the central place where all route groups are registered. The server is built with `createServer()` which chains `.use()` calls:

```typescript
app.use(projectMiddleware)
   .get('/api/health', ...)
   .use(createTasksRoutes({ pubsub }))
   .use(createItemsRoutes())
   .use(createInboxRoutes({ pubsub }))
   .use(createMetaRoutes())
   .use(createTriageRoutes({ pubsub }))
   .use(createValidationRoutes())
   .use(createProjectsRoutes({ projectManager }))
   .use(createSessionRoutes())
   .use(createPlansRoutes())
   .use(createAgentDispatchRoutes({ pubsub }))
   .ws('/ws', { ... })
```

---

### All Route Files

| File | Prefix | Methods |
|------|--------|---------|
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts` | `/api/tasks` | GET, POST |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/items.ts` | `/api/items` | GET only |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/inbox.ts` | `/api/inbox` | GET, POST, DELETE |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts` | `/api/meta` | GET only |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/triage.ts` | `/api/triage` | GET, POST |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/validation.ts` | `/api` (search/validate/alignment) | GET only |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/projects.ts` | `/api/projects` | GET, POST, DELETE |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/sessions.ts` | `/api/sessions` | GET only |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/plans.ts` | `/api/plans` | GET only |
| `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/agent-dispatch.ts` | `/api/agent` | GET, POST |

---

### All Data-Modifying Endpoints (POST/DELETE)

**Tasks** (`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/tasks.ts`):
- `POST /api/tasks/:ref/start` — transitions task to `in_progress`
- `POST /api/tasks/:ref/note` — appends a note (body: `{ content: string }`)
- `POST /api/tasks/:ref/submit` — transitions to `pending_review`
- `POST /api/tasks/:ref/complete` — transitions to `completed` (body: `{ reason: string }`)
- `POST /api/tasks/:ref/block` — transitions to `blocked` (body: `{ reason: string }`)

**Inbox** (`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/inbox.ts`):
- `POST /api/inbox` — creates a new inbox item (body: `{ text: string, tags?: string[], added_by?: string }`)
- `DELETE /api/inbox/:ref` — deletes an inbox item by ref

**Triage** (`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/triage.ts`):
- `POST /api/triage` — records a triage decision (body: `{ inbox_ref, action, reasoning, decided_by?, evidence_refs? }`)
- `POST /api/triage/:ref/override` — overrides a prior decision (body: `{ action, reasoning, override_by? }`)
- `POST /api/triage/:ref/act` — executes the triage action (no body)

**Projects** (`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/projects.ts`):

It doesn't have a native `.patch()` — use `.post()` for mutations consistent with existing patterns. --- ### 5. {actionError}

` - Read-only guard: `{#if !isStaticMode()} ... {/if}` - Action handler pattern: ```typescript async function handleAction(action: () => Promise) { isSubmitting = true; actionError = ''; try { await action(); await reloadAndNotify(); } catch (err) { actionError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Action failed'; } finally { isSubmitting = false; } } ``` **Dialog sub-components:** - `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/components/ui/dialog/dialog-content.svelte` — built on `bits-ui`, `DialogPrimitive.Content`, fixed center, `max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] sm:max-w-lg`, auto close button top-right - The dialog content supports `class` prop for overriding max-width (e.g. `max-w-2xl` used in TaskDetailModal) **Inbox page** uses Dialog for delete confirmation: `deleteConfirmOpen = $state(false)` — simpler pattern with `Dialog` imported directly from `$lib/components/ui/dialog`. --- ### 7. API Client Patterns **File:** `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/src/lib/api.ts` All API calls follow this pattern: ```typescript export async function someMutation(ref: string, data: SomeType): Promise { assertWritable('action name'); // throws ReadOnlyModeError in static mode const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/api/some/endpoint`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...getProjectHeaders() // adds X-Kspec-Dir header if project selected }, body: JSON.stringify(data) }); if (!response.ok) { await handleResponseError(response); // throws Error with message from response JSON } return response.json(); } ``` Key helpers: - `getProjectHeaders()` — returns `{ 'X-Kspec-Dir': path }` if a project is selected (from `getSelectedProjectPath()`) - `handleResponseError(response)` — parses `{ message, error }` JSON body, calls `clearInvalidSelection()` if needed, then `throw new Error(message)` - `assertWritable(action)` — from `$lib/stores/mode.svelte`, throws `ReadOnlyModeError` in static mode - `isStaticMode()` — returns true for GitHub Pages export mode - `DAEMON_API_BASE` — from `$lib/constants`, typically `http://localhost:3456` The `AgentDefinition` interface (lines 620-645) maps to what the daemon returns from `GET /api/meta/agents`. It does NOT include `automation`, `tags`, `prompt_template`, `session_protocol`, or `conventions` — these would need to be added to the interface if used in an edit form. --- ### 8. Meta Set Infrastructure in the Daemon There is **no existing `PATCH /api/meta/agents/:id`** endpoint. The CLI `kspec meta set ` command (in `src/cli/commands/meta.ts` lines 1545-1719) does the mutation server-side via: 1. `resolveMetaRef(metaCtx, ref)` — finds the agent by id/ULID 2. Mutates the agent object in memory 3. `saveMetaItem(ctx, found, 'agent')` — writes to `kynetic.meta.yaml` via `writeYamlFilePreserveFormat` 4. `commitIfShadow(ctx.shadow, ...)` — commits to the shadow branch The daemon `src/parser/meta.ts` provides: - `saveMetaItem(ctx, item, itemType)` — generic upsert for agents/workflows/conventions/skills - `loadMetaContext(ctx)` — loads all meta with includes - `findMetaManifest(specDir)` — discovers `kynetic.meta.yaml` - `resolveMetaRef(meta, ref)` — resolves by ULID, short ULID, or `id` field To add a PATCH/update agent endpoint to the daemon, you would add it to `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/daemon/src/routes/meta.ts` following the existing Elysia pattern, importing `saveMetaItem` from the parser, and calling `commitIfShadow` after mutation.

## Test Infrastructure Overview

Two separate testing frameworks are used, clearly separated by concern:

2. **Playwright** - E2E tests. Config at `/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/playwright.config.ts`. `testDir` is `./tests/e2e`, workers=1 (sequential), no shared `baseURL` (each test gets its own ephemeral-port daemon).

There is no `@testing-library/svelte` or DOM-based component testing. Component behavior is validated either through E2E Playwright tests or static source-file analysis.

### 1. Agent-Related Tests in `packages/web-ui/`

**E2E Playwright test (agents page UI):**
`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/agents.spec.ts`

Tests the `/agents` page rendered in browser. Covers:
- `data-testid="agent-card-{id}"` per agent (e.g. `agent-card-task-worker`)
- `data-testid="agent-name"`, `agent-trigger"`, `agent-active-count"`, `agent-completed-count"` inside each card

- Accessibility: `aria-live` regions (`invocation-live-region`, `active-invocations-section`)
- Navigation: sidebar link `nav-link-agents`

Pattern example:
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '../fixtures/test-base';

test('renders agent cards from meta definitions', async ({ page, daemon }) => {
  await page.goto('/agents');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('agents-loading')).toHaveCount(0);
  const card = page.getByTestId('agent-card-task-worker');
  await expect(card).toBeVisible();
});
```

**E2E Playwright test (agent dispatch API):**
`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/api-agent-dispatch.spec.ts`

Calls the daemon HTTP API directly (not the browser). Covers:

- Legacy `POST /api/agent/dispatch/start` and `/stop` routes

- `GET /api/meta/workflows` - paginated `{items, total}`

`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/api-tasks.spec.ts`
Covers:
- `GET /api/tasks` - paginated `{items, total, offset, limit}`, required fields

- `GET /api/tasks/:ref` - full task with notes, todos, deps

### 3. Unit Tests in `packages/web-ui/tests/`

These two vitest files live directly in `packages/web-ui/tests/` (not under `e2e/`) and run with vitest:

**Board utilities:**
`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tests/board-utils.test.ts`

Uses `import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'`. Tests pure utility functions from `src/lib/components/board/board-utils`. No mocking, no DOM. Example:

### 4. Root-Level Static Analysis Tests (run via `npm test` in web-ui)

The web-ui `package.json` `test` script runs these three vitest tests from the project root:

`/home/chapel/Projects/kynetic-spec-ui/packages/web-ui/tests/fixtures/test-base.ts`
